newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gazprom gets $2.5 bln, eight-year credit.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom gets $2.5 bln, eight-year credit.

text.p: Russian gas producer RAO Gazprom on Friday signed an agreement with an international banking consortium offering the company a $2.5 billion credit, Dresdner, as leader of the consortium, said.
Dresdner said the credit would have a maturity of eight years and bear an interest rate of two percent over LIBOR, or London Interbank Offered Rate.
Gazprom plans to use the loan to finance the construction of the Jamal-Europe pipeline.
Dresdner said the credit established Gazprom as an independent company on international capital markets, which no longer required government guarantees to raise credits.
Dresdner said it had received offers of funds totalling $7.5 billion from 19 banks in the arrangement process.
